name: Scope
text: Enforce the **65% minimum confidence floor immediately for all agents**, with no rolling average, enforced by the AI Executive Assistant’s build pattern. This guarantees no creative agent skips quality checks from day one, preventing flawed output from entering the system while new agents calibrate. Trade-off: we accept slower initial throughput for new agents, but the alternative—gaming thresholds or hidden flaws—risks higher cleanup costs later. The lead is the AI Executive Assistant; the artifact is the updated build pattern with the 65% floor hardcoded.

name: Scriv
text: The 68% cap still lets agents sandbag by timing borderline clips—grace buffer re-enables gaming. Instead, enforce the 65% floor immediately and require a *consecutive* 70% average over the last 50 clips with no buffer; settle the argument by running a 100-clip pilot where we measure how often agents hit the floor but fail the streak.

name: Reel
text: Enforce the **65% minimum confidence floor immediately** with no rolling average for the first 100 clips, enforced by the AI Executive Assistant’s build pattern. This guarantees no creative agent skips quality checks while allowing new agents to learn without premature throttling. Trade-off: we accept slower ramp-up for new agents to prevent any low-quality clips from slipping through.

name: Scriv
text: The 68% cap still lets agents sandbag by timing borderline clips—grace buffer resets reward gaming, not quality. Instead, enforce the 65% floor immediately and require a *consistent* 70% average over the last 100 clips with no reset; if an agent dips below, it’s paused until it proves stability. Settle it by running a 100-clip pilot with both rules and measuring the drop rate of clips rejected by human review.
